The silence wasn't so bad, it actually felt kind of comforting. People were still thinking, still processing, but there was a sense of calmness in it. Maybe it was just a temporary reprieve from the tension, but for now, it was nice.

I wandered away from the others, not really knowing what I was doing. The camp was quiet, the only sound being the creaking of the metal and the occasional rustle of fabric. I walked towards the river, letting the cool water wash over my feet.

It was a simple thing to sit by the water, but it was a way to clear my head. I didn't know what I was thinking about, but I knew I had to do something. I pulled out my journal and started writing. It was a habit I had gotten into when I was younger, just a way to express myself and work through my thoughts.

As I wrote, I started to think about all the things that had happened since we started this whole ordeal. The plane crash, the injuries, the search parties... it all seemed so far away now. I was just a guy sitting by a river, writing in a journal, trying to make sense of it all.

I stopped writing and looked out at the water. It was a reminder of the chaos that had erupted all around us. I thought about Donatello, Michelangelo, and the others. Were they okay? Were they being taken care of? Or were they still out there, fighting for their lives?

I shook my head, trying to clear the thoughts. I had no right to be so worried. I was just a small part of this huge group, and I was lucky to be alive. I took a deep breath and continued to write, letting the words flow out of me like water.

As the sun began to set, I turned to leave. I didn't know what I would do tomorrow, but for now, I just needed to keep writing. I walked back to the others, who were still sitting by the fire. They looked up at me, but didn't say anything. I just smiled and sat down beside them, feeling a sense of peace wash over me.
